absent: Locking discipline and concurrency guarantees for control-block updates, identifier allocation and debug state changes.
Complete memory layout of control block, save area and segment descriptors beyond observed fields.
Semantics of nested permission validation, guest page validation and nested control-block mapping failure handling.
Full userspace contract for debug, shutdown and internal-error exits beyond observed payload fields.
Behavior of port I/O completion callbacks, emulator port helpers and encrypted-guest string I/O path.
Detailed machine-check processing, translation flush scope and erratum handling beyond observed signature test.

findings.text: Global invalid-opcode entry point validates whether emulation may proceed, recognizes an optional forced-emulation signature at the guest instruction pointer with optional flag adjustment and pointer advance, then delegates to the common instruction emulator with either normal or forced trap type.
Global guest-virtual reader offers virtually addressed guest memory reads with access privilege derived from current privilege level and a cleared exception record contract.
Global fast port I/O dispatcher selects input versus output handling by direction flag and advances past the emulated instruction when the selected path reports completion.

Global task-switch entry point refuses emulation when control-extension protections are active, otherwise initializes emulation context and reports internal emulation failure to userspace on error or when memory-mapped I/O would be required, else commits new instruction pointer and flags.
Global buffer-based emulation entry point emulates an instruction image supplied by the caller for a given length through the common x86 emulator.

Header inline machine-check helper is a no-op without machine-check support, otherwise synthesizes host register state with user code segment and interrupt flag set before invoking host machine-check handling.

Segment state written to the control block preserves base, limit and selector verbatim while descriptor attributes combine type, descriptor kind, privilege, presence combined with usability, and availability plus mode and granularity flags; stack-segment updates additionally mirror privilege into saved current privilege, and the segment portion is marked dirty.
Breakpoint interception is enabled exactly when guest debugging is active with software breakpoint use requested, otherwise it remains cleared.

Address-space identifier allocation uses per-CPU generation counting with wrap to minimum and a flag requesting global flush on exhaustion; each virtual CPU records current generation and receives a monotonically increasing identifier.

Debug status and control writes are ignored for guests with protected state; otherwise status updates occur only on change and control updates always commit, with the debug portion marked dirty on modification.

Dirty debug register synchronization is prohibited for encrypted-state guests, otherwise it captures hardware breakpoints into architecture state, mirrors saved status and control values, clears the no-exit optimization flag, and refreshes intercept configuration.

Page-fault exit entry extracts fault address and error code from exit information fields and forwards them to the common page-fault handler, supplying decoded instruction bytes only when decode assistance is available.

Debug and breakpoint exits distinguish userspace reporting from guest reinjection based on single-step, hardware-breakpoint and single-step-after-nonmaskable-interrupt state; userspace reports carry status, control, linear program counter and vector, while unclaimed debug faults are reinjected with a payload derived from saved status, and short breakpoint traps advance past the instruction before raising debug fault.

Several exit entries act as narrow delegates: invalid-opcode exits forward to the global undefined handler, alignment faults queue an alignment exception without extra error information, machine-check, nonmaskable and system-management exits request host resumption, and generic exits invoke the common emulator.

Virtual guest reads proceed page by page through the walker translation, abort with fault propagation on invalid translation, suspend for I/O on guest page read failure, and correctly handle ranges spanning page boundaries.

Machine-check handling first tests for a specific processor erratum via status signature comparison after masking reserved bits, clearing status registers and flushing translation caches on match; erratum match requests guest termination while other cases invoke host machine-check processing.

Shutdown exits report a shutdown reason to userspace; for non-encrypted guests the control block is cleared and virtual CPU state reset with system-management notification when applicable, while encrypted-state guests skip reinitialization because save state is already protected.

Port I/O exits decode string versus individual transfer, direction, port number and operand size from exit information and count the exit; string transfers use encrypted-guest special handling or generic emulation, individual transfers record next instruction pointer and use fast paths that complete kernel-handled cases or park for userspace with recorded linear address and completion callbacks, including distinct handling for a legacy compatibility port when its quirk is enabled, with input merging preserving prior accumulator contents for narrow sizes.

Nested virtual-machine load, save and run exits enforce permission checks and address validation with general-protection injection on failure, map the nested control block with memory-failure handling, advance past the instruction, and copy load-save state between host and nested blocks in the direction indicated by the operation, clearing high system-call state on load; run exits delegate to nested run handling after permission checks.

Decoded-instruction exit classification accepts only short virtualization opcodes and distinguishes run, load and save operations by distinct final encoding bytes, returning neutral value otherwise, with compile-time assurance that exit codes are valid.

General-protection exits carrying error information unconditionally reinject; cases lacking such information decode the faulting instruction to detect virtualization operations for direct handling in host context or permission-checked synthesis of nested exits in guest context, otherwise optionally emulate a hypervisor backdoor for top-level guests when enabled, with all other cases reinjecting the fault.
Global-interrupt-flag exits for set and clear share permission validation and instruction advance, differing only in the flag value installed.

Address-space invalidation exits treat extended invalidation with address-space identifier as page invalidation using guest virtual address from accumulator state, secure-init exits are reported as undefined opcode, and page-invalidation exits use hardware-provided address with decode assistance or fall back to generic emulation.

Task-switch exits derive selector, reason and error information from exit fields, distinguishing return, jump, gate and call origins and clearing pending nonmaskable, exception or interrupt state for gate switches according to event type, with selective instruction advance for non-gate and software or benign fault cases before delegating to common task-switch emulation.

Interrupt-return interception management excludes encrypted-state guests from changes; the intercept entry records window-exit statistics, arms awaiting-completion state, captures return address, disables further interception, and requests event processing.
System-management resume exits emulate from a short fixed-length instruction image through the buffer-based emulator.

Observed control-block usage includes segment descriptors with base, limit, selector and attribute storage, save area holding privilege level, debug status and control, instruction pointer and code base, and control area holding exit codes, error and address information plus instruction bytes and length; userspace debug reporting carries status, control, linear program counter and vector.

Encrypted-state guests forbid direct debug-register synchronization, interrupt-return interception changes, shutdown reinitialization and generic string I/O, requiring specialized paths or skipping operations to avoid touching protected or encrypted state.

Task switching cannot be emulated when control-flow enforcement extensions are active or when memory-mapped I/O would be required, in which cases an internal emulation error is reported; a specific hardware erratum match during machine-check handling terminates the guest via triple fault rather than resuming.

Userspace debug exit payload is defined as status and control debug values plus linear program counter computed from code base and instruction pointer plus fault vector distinguishing debug trap from breakpoint trap.

Port I/O exit encoding packs string flag, direction, size and port number into exit information with next instruction pointer in a separate field; resume-from-management emulation uses a short fixed length; virtualization opcode classification uses a fixed short length with distinct final bytes for run, load and save.
